title_after: [RETIRED 2026-08-22] Croatian Listening Pods — Laura & Mark dialogues (never learner-facing)

before.known_text: Morning! Awful weather out there, isn't it?
Don't tell me. I got completely soaked just walking from the station.
Was the train late again?
Ten minutes, and packed like sardines in a can. Apparently there was a signal problem.
Typical Monday. I came by car this time, and the traffic was a nightmare.
I don't blame you, in this weather. I nearly took the bus instead.
Why didn't you?
I was about thirty seconds late. I watched it leave and everything.
That's the worst feeling.
It really is. Anyway, coffee first, I think, before I do anything else.
Good plan. I badly need one.
Same time tomorrow, probably just as wet.
Don't say that. I can't cope with two days of this kind of weather.
Good morning! How was your weekend?
Really good, thanks. On Saturday we went to the sea.
Oh, lovely. What was the weather like?
Beautiful in the morning. But in the afternoon it rained, so we found a small café and we just sat there for two hours.
That sounds really nice, actually.
It was. The kids weren't happy, though. They wanted to swim.
Did they go in the sea in the end?
They did, on Sunday morning. It was freezing, but they liked it. And what about you? Did you do anything?
Not much, honestly. I was really tired after last week, so I stayed home and read my book.
Which book?
The one about the lighthouse — I told you about it. I finished it last night.
Was it good?
I really liked it. I cried at the end, actually. You can borrow it if you want.
Go on then. I need something for the train.
Are you doing anything on Saturday?
On Saturday… I'm taking my mum shopping in the morning, but I'm free after that. Why?
A few of us are going to that new place by the river for lunch. Do you want to come?
The one with the green tables? I've been wanting to try it for ages.
That's the one. We're thinking about one o'clock.
One might be a bit tight for me. Could we say half past?
Half past should be fine. I'll check with the others and let you know.
Perfect. Shall I book a table? It gets busy at the weekend.
Good idea. There'll be five of us — six if Katie comes.
I'll book for six, just in case. What's Katie doing these days? I haven't seen her since the summer.
She's been really busy — she started a new job last month. She'll tell you all about it on Saturday.
I look forward to it. Right, I'd better go. See you Saturday.
See you then. I'll text you when I've spoken to the others.
Is this your sister? You look really alike.
That's Grace, yes. Everyone says that, but I think she's more like my mum.
How much older is she than you?
Only two years. We used to fight like cat and dog, but now we're really close.
And who's this other one, in the blue jumper?
That's my youngest sister, Millie. She's twelve years old, so she's a lot younger than us.
Is she like either of you?
She's more like Grace, actually — she's quiet and really good at school. I was always the loud one.
And the dog?
That's Biscuit. He's technically Grace's, but he spends half his life at my place.
He's huge. What breed is he?
Some kind of retriever. He's as soft as anything, but he's completely useless as a guard dog.
Sounds like the perfect family, honestly.
Most of the time. Millie's the difficult one now, not me, which feels like justice to me.
You don't look good. Are you okay?
Honestly, not really. My throat has been hurting since yesterday.
You should go home, Sam. You look exhausted.
But I've got that meeting at eleven. I don't want to let anyone down.
I can take over the meeting. It's really not a big deal.
Are you sure? I feel uncomfortable asking.
You're not asking, I'm offering. Go home, rest, drink something warm.
Thank you. I think I'll really take your advice.
Have you taken something for it?
Just paracetamol this morning. It hasn't really helped.
Try honey and lemon when you get home. My mum swears by it.
Honestly, I think I'll just go straight to bed.
Good idea. Send me a message later and let me know how you're feeling.
I will. Thank you for covering for me, I really appreciate it.
So, how's the new job going? You've been there, what, a month now?
Six weeks, actually. And honestly, so much better than the last place.
Really? In what way?
The people, mostly. Everyone's friendly, and my manager actually listens when I say something's not working.
That makes such a difference. Your old boss sounded like a nightmare.
He really was. I used to dread Monday mornings there.
And the work itself? Is it what you expected?
More or less. It's busier than I thought, but a good busy, if that makes sense.
It does. Are you still doing the same hours?
A bit more flexible, actually. I can start later if I need to.
That would suit you. You were never a morning person.
Never. Honestly, I think I made the right move leaving.
I'm really glad. You deserve it after everything last year.
Thanks. It feels good to actually enjoy going to work again.
So you saw the new flat yesterday? How was it?
Really good, actually. It's much bigger than my current flat.
That's great. What's it like, exactly?
Two bedrooms, a proper kitchen, and it also has a little balcony.
Sounds perfect. Is there a flaw?
There's always a flaw. It doesn't have much light, especially in the afternoon.
That's a shame. Would that really bother you?
I think it would, over winter. I love when the sun comes in while I'm working from home.
And what about the location? Is it convenient?
Much closer to work, which is a big advantage. I'd save about half an hour a day.
That's not unimportant. So, more space and less light, but a shorter journey to work.
Exactly so. I'm still not sure what matters more to me.
I would probably take the extra space, personally. You can always turn on a lamp.
True. I think I'm leaning that way too, if I'm honest.
Go on, show me some photos from the trip.
Okay, here — this is the beach near the hotel.
That water looks incredible. Was it really that blue?
Honestly, even bluer in real life. We swam there every morning.
Who's this with you?
That's my cousin, Dan. He came for the last few days.
And this one? You're both completely wet, laughing.
Oh, that was right after the boat ride. We got completely soaked.
Was that the day you saw the dolphins?
That's the one. We almost missed them, actually — I was looking the wrong way.
And this last one?
That's just the view from our balcony at sunset. I took about fifty of that exact photo.
I don't blame you. It's beautiful.
Okay, that's enough photos for today. I could talk about that holiday forever.
Did you watch that film in the end, the one everyone's talking about?
I did, last night. I really liked it. I nearly cried at the ending.
Really? I thought it was just okay.
Just okay? Come on, the acting alone was incredible.
The acting was good, I'll give you that. I just thought the story was a bit slow.
I didn't think so. I thought it built up really nicely, right up to the end.
Maybe I wasn't in the right mood for it, then.
Probably. What did you watch instead, before this one?
Something much lighter, an old comedy. I needed a break after a long week.
Fair enough. We can't always agree on everything.
No, we clearly can't. Still, I'm glad you liked it.
You should give it another chance sometime, honestly. Maybe on a better day.
Maybe I will. Though I still think you're wrong about the pacing.
We'll just have to agree to disagree on that one.
Where did you actually grow up? You've never really said.
A small town by the sea, in the north. You wouldn't have heard of it.
Try me.
It doesn't matter, honestly, it's tiny. We used to go down to the harbour every single evening after school.
That sounds lovely. What was there to do, though, in a place that small?
Not much, if I'm honest. We used to just sit on the wall and watch the boats come in.
Did you ever get bored?
Constantly. But I didn't realise it at the time — it just felt normal.
Is your family still there?
My parents are, yes. My dad still walks down to the harbour every morning, actually.
And do you miss it?
More than I thought I would. I used to want to leave so badly.
Funny how that changes.
It really is. I go back every summer now, and I love it more each time.
Tell me about the trip, then. Did anything go wrong?
One thing, actually, and it was completely my fault. On the first day we got on the wrong bus.
Oh no. How did that happen?
We were tired from the flight, and I just read the number wrong. We ended up about an hour outside the city before we even noticed.
An hour! What did you do?
We just laughed, honestly, once we'd got over the panic. There was nothing else to do.
Did you have to pay for another bus back?
We did, and it took most of the afternoon we'd planned for the old town. Completely wasted, really.
That's annoying. Did it put you off for the rest of the trip?
Not at all, actually. We ended up in this tiny village we'd otherwise never have seen, and had the best coffee of the whole holiday.
So it worked out, in the end.
Yes, it did. Now it's the story we tell everyone, more than about the places we actually meant to visit.
It's funny how it's always the mistakes that make the best stories.
Every time. I wouldn't change it, honestly, even that hour on the wrong bus.
You're learning something new, aren't you? Didn't you mention that a while back?
I am, yes. I actually started learning the guitar a couple of months ago.
How's it going?
Slowly. But I try to do a little every day, even just ten minutes.
I think that's the right way. Better than one big session a week.
That's what I'm at least hoping for. I can play a few chords now, at least that.
What prompted you to start?
Honestly, I always wanted to, but before I never had the time. Now I've simply decided to make time.
Do you have a teacher, or are you doing it by yourself?
A bit of both. I watch videos online, and I have a lesson once every two weeks.
That sounds like a good balance. Are there any songs you're working on?
There's one I really love, but it's still far beyond my reach. I'm hoping to learn it by Christmas, maybe.
I believe it. You always finish what you start.
I hope so. Ask me again in a few months and we'll see.
I've got some news, actually. Are you sitting down?
That sounds serious. Go on, then.
We got the house! The one by the park, the one we've been looking for for months.
You're joking! That's amazing, Katie, congratulations.
Honestly, I still can't quite believe it. We only found out an hour ago.
When are you moving in?
Not until September, but still. I've already started thinking about wall colours.
Of course you have. Will you have a party when you move in?
Definitely. You'll be the first one invited.
I'll hold you to that. Is Mark as excited as you are?
More, actually. He's already looked up which bus goes past the park.
That's so like him. Well, I'm really happy for you both.
Thank you. It's been a few long months of waiting, so this feels incredible.
You deserve it. Right, this definitely calls for a celebration.
